# Results — Study 777 (Black-Friday-Retail)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
**retail (XRT) rallies into Black-Friday week**: the SPDR S&P Retail ETF is bid up ahead
of the biggest US shopping day (the Friday after Thanksgiving), then fades once the
Cyber-week numbers are out. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last
complete calendar month). Fingerprint `75498c2542dd` (XRT + SPY, one combined panel,
adjusted/total-return daily closes).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (total-return) closes, `XRT` (SPDR S&P Retail ETF) + `SPY` (S&P 500), one combined panel: 5,036 rows, 2006-06-22 → 2026-06-30 |
| Calendar | **hardcoded**: 20 Black Fridays 2006→2025, each the day after the fourth Thursday of November (US Thanksgiving); fixed by statute, cross-checked vs the NYSE holiday calendar. Black Friday is a half session (1pm ET close) but a real trading day |
| Events resolvable | all **20** of 20 Black Fridays have XRT+SPY coverage around the anchor |
| Statistics | one-sample *t* of the abnormal return (XRT − SPY) across independent, non-overlapping yearly events (the correct unit — not a daily panel); Wilson hit-rate interval; a 20-seed × 200-draw random-window placebo per cut; leave-one-out jackknife |
| Execution / costs | **calendar-known, zero look-ahead**: the Black-Friday date is fixed years ahead. Run-up = [anchor−K → anchor]; fade = [anchor → anchor+K]; net of 2× one-way cost × NAV. Gross AND net reported |
| Price basis | **total-return** (dividends reinvested, `auto_adjust=True`) for both legs |

**Beta, named:** XRT is an equal-weighted sector ETF with a market beta near 1, so a raw
`XRT − SPY` difference over a drifting window is only mildly mechanical; we quote the
*abnormal* return throughout so the November-seasonal drift of the broad tape is netted
out and only retail's *relative* move remains.

## The run-up — abnormal return, K sessions BEFORE Black Friday (XRT − SPY)

| cut | n | mean AR | *t* | hit rate (Wilson 95%) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2-week run-up (k=10) | 20 | **+1.333%** | **+1.585** | 13/20 = 65.0% [43.3%, 81.9%] |
| 1-month run-up (k=21) | 20 | +1.138% | +1.086 | 12/20 = 60.0% [38.7%, 78.1%] |

Unlike most of the calendar-folklore studies, the run-up here points the *right* way: in
the two weeks into Black Friday XRT has, on average, *out*-performed SPY by +1.33%, hit
13 of 20 years — a genuine mild tilt in the folklore's direction. But the cross-year
*t* is only **+1.59** (year-to-year variance is large), it does not clear the desk's
significance bar, and it **weakens** as you stretch the window to a month (+1.14%,
*t* = +1.1). A directional whiff, not a robust effect.

## The fade — abnormal return, K sessions AFTER Black Friday

| cut | n | mean AR | *t* | hit rate (Wilson 95%) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2-week fade (k=10) | 20 | +0.059% | +0.081 | 9/20 = 45.0% [25.8%, 65.8%] |
| 1-month fade (k=21) | 20 | −0.497% | −0.435 | 9/20 = 45.0% [25.8%, 65.8%] |

The "sell the news" half is a **clean zero**: post-Black-Friday XRT is statistically
indistinguishable from SPY (both cuts |*t*| < 0.5). There is no reliable fade to short —
the "buy the rumour, *sell the news*" story is only half a story, and the sold half is
absent.

## Random-window placebo (20 seeds × 200 draws per event)

| cut | tail | observed | placebo mean (sd) | p |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2-week run-up | right | +1.333% | −0.012% (0.667%) | 0.0262 |
| 2-week fade | left | +0.059% | −0.012% (0.667%) | 0.5457 |

The 2-week run-up sits in the **right tail** of the luck cloud (right-tail p = 0.026 ⇒
only ~2.6% of random 2-week XRT-vs-SPY windows were this positive) — so the pre-Black-
Friday pop is *not* ordinary tracking noise. Note the tension with the one-sample *t*:
the placebo pools every draw into a tight null (sd of the mean 0.67%), so it flags the
window as unusual, while the cross-year *t* (which pays the full year-to-year variance)
is only +1.59. Both are honest; the effect is real-ish but small and noisy. The fade is
dead-centre (p = 0.55).

## Jackknife (leave-one-out) — 2-week run-up *t*

Full-sample *t* = **+1.585**; across all 20 leave-one-out draws the *t* stays in
**[+1.167, +2.145]** — the run-up is **not** driven by a single year (e.g. one huge
holiday-hope rally); it is a broad, if small, positive tilt that never quite reaches
significance and is never carried by one outlier.

## Tradability — net of costs (calendar-known entry, zero look-ahead)

| window | gross | net @ 5 bps | net @ 10 bps |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2-week run-up | +1.333% (*t* +1.59) | +1.233% (*t* +1.47) | +1.133% (*t* +1.35) |
| 2-week fade | +0.059% (*t* +0.08) | −0.041% (*t* −0.06) | −0.141% (*t* −0.20) |

The run-up is a *long* in a liquid sector ETF, so it survives costs almost intact
(+1.23% net @ 5 bps) and capacity is not the problem. The problem is the *edge itself*:
a +1.3%/yr once-a-year window with a cross-year *t* of ~1.6 is not statistically
reliable — it is one positive cut inside a four-window search (two horizons × run-up/fade),
and the "sell the news" fade it is supposed to pair with is a clean zero. Nothing you can
bank on.

## Synthetic positive control (deterministic, no network)

- **Null (bump = 0), 20 seeds:** mean *t* = −0.59 (sd 1.49); |*t*| ≥ 2 in **3/20** seeds —
  the honest small-sample false-positive rate at n = 20 events with a 10-day AR is
  elevated (~15%), a caution flag against over-reading any single ~1.6 *t*.
- **Planted run-up +1.0% (seed 783):** mean AR +2.47%, *t* = **+3.72**.
- **Planted run-up +2.0% (seed 783):** mean AR +3.47%, *t* = **+5.23** — a real bump is
  recovered monotonically, so a genuine pre-Black-Friday rally of that size would have
  shown up loudly. The observed +1.33% (*t* +1.59) is well below that.

## Verdict

| Axis | Stamp | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Signal — is the effect real?** | **Weak** | The run-up points the *right* way — XRT beats SPY by +1.33% into Black Friday, hits 13/20 years, sits in the placebo right tail (p ≈ 0.026), and the jackknife stays positive. That is a genuine, directionally-correct whiff — more than most calendar folklore delivers. But the cross-year *t* is only +1.59 (below significance), it **weakens** at a 1-month lookback, the "sell the news" fade is a clean zero, and the synthetic null fires |*t*| ≥ 2 on 3/20 seeds at this n. Suggestive, not robust. |
| **Tradability — survives costs/scale?** | **Mirage** | Nothing to bank. Net of costs the run-up is +1.2%/yr with *t* ≈ 1.5 — one positive cut inside a four-window search, no reliable statistical edge, and its partner "fade" trade doesn't exist. Liquid and long (capacity is fine), but there is no dependable signal to size. |

**In one sentence:** retail *does* drift up into Black-Friday week — by about +1.3% vs the
market over the prior fortnight, the right direction and unusual vs random windows — but
the effect is small, only marginally significant (*t* ≈ 1.6), fades at a longer lookback,
and comes with no "sell the news" reversal, so it is a suggestive curiosity, not a
bankable trade.
